transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Did you have any questions about your surgery or recovery that I can help with today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to our guidelines, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's essential to avoid any strenuous activities, lifting heavy objects, or bending for a month. Also, please be careful not to get any water or debris in your eyes while gardening. Do you have any other questions about your recovery or gardening?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that sounds good. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP can provide more. It's safe to use preservative-free eye drops four times a day to help with dryness. Have any other questions about your recovery or eye care?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I am also curious because I’m very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to feel a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in bright conditions. You might find it helpful to wear sunglasses when you're outside. If the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to assess it further. Otherwise, it's usually just a matter of adjusting to your new eyes. Do you have any other questions about your recovery?
transcript.delivered: It's normal to feel a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in bright conditions. You might find it helpful to wear sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thanks. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. Have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all I have for now. Thank you for answering my questions!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: All your questions have been answered. .
